F1.1.1.q: A free torch app collects users' location and contacts and sells them to advertisers without asking. Which ethical issue does this raise?
F1.1.1.why: Privacy is a person's right to control how their personal information is collected, used and shared.

F1.1.2.q: A company replaces every staff laptop each year and sends the old ones to landfill. Which ethical issue is this?
F1.1.2.why: E-waste, energy use and manufacturing emissions are the environmental impact of IT.

F1.1.3.q: A council moves all parking permit applications online only. Elderly residents without internet or IT skills can no longer apply. Which issue is this?
F1.1.3.why: The digital divide is the gap between those with devices, internet and skills and those without.

F1.1.4.q: A visually impaired employee is refused a screen reader, so they cannot use the company's systems. Which ethical issue is this?
F1.1.4.why: Disabled people should have fair access to the assistive technology they need.

F1.1.5.q: A group of students repeatedly posts insulting comments about a classmate on social media. Which issue is this?
F1.1.5.why: Cyberbullying and trolling break the standards of respectful online behaviour.

F1.1.6.q: Before getting a login, new staff must sign a document saying they won't share passwords or install unapproved software. What is this document?
F1.1.6.why: An AUP sets out what users may and may not do on an organisation's IT systems.

F2.1.1.q: A former employee uses an old password to log into his ex-employer's customer database without permission. Which law has he broken?
F2.1.1.why: Unauthorised access to computer material is a Section 1 offence under the Computer Misuse Act.

F2.1.1.q: A hacker breaks into a bank's system in order to transfer money to himself. Under the Computer Misuse Act, what makes this more serious than simply logging in?
options: Access with intent to commit a further crime (Section 2)
Failing to report a breach in 72 hours
F2.1.1.why: Section 2 covers unauthorised access with intent to commit or help commit a further offence, such as fraud.

F2.1.2.q: A student downloads a pirated copy of a paid film and shares it with friends. Which law does this break?
F2.1.2.why: The CDPA protects creators' work from being copied or shared without permission.

F2.1.3.q: A developer copies another company's source code and sells the program as their own. Which regulations specifically protect the program as a literary work?
F2.1.3.why: The 1992 regulations extend copyright to computer programs as literary works.

F2.1.4.q: A call-centre worker gets back pain and eye strain from long shifts at a screen. What do the regulations require her employer to provide?
options: Adjustable chairs, eye tests and screen breaks
A data breach report within 72 hours
F2.1.4.why: The DSE Regulations require employers to protect staff who use screens regularly.

F2.1.5.q: A GP surgery's records are hacked and patient data is stolen. Under data protection law, how quickly must the breach be reported to the ICO?
F2.1.5.why: UK GDPR requires serious personal data breaches to be reported within 72 hours.

F2.1.5.q: An online shop keeps old customers' details for ten years 'just in case', with no reason to. Which law does this break?
F2.1.5.why: Personal data must not be kept longer than necessary for its purpose.
